title: Fluvial, Glacial and Aeolian Landforms

cards.b: Landforms are made by agents of gradation: running water, ice, wind, waves and groundwater. UPSC asks you to name a landform, say which agent made it and where it is found. If you link each landform to its agent and stage, you can answer almost any question in this area.

Each agent works in two steps: erosion (wearing away) and deposition (laying down). Rivers cut V-shaped valleys. Glaciers cut U-shaped valleys. Wind cuts hollows and builds dunes. The shape of the valley is the quickest clue to the agent.

Remember: agents work best in specific climates. Rivers dominate humid regions, ice dominates cold and high regions, wind dominates dry regions.

cards.h: River stages: youth, maturity, old age
cards.b:
W M Davis proposed the cycle of erosion in 1899. In youth the river cuts down: waterfalls, rapids, gorges and V-shaped valleys. In maturity it widens its valley and forms meanders. In old age it deposits: floodplains, levees, oxbow lakes, deltas.

Critics say the cycle is too tidy. Real rivers can show all stages at once and tectonic uplift can restart the cycle. This is called rejuvenation.

Waterfalls form where a hard rock layer overlies soft rock. Potholes are drilled by swirling pebbles. Gorges and canyons form in dry, uplifted rock (Grand Canyon on the Colorado). River terraces are old floodplains left high after uplift. Incised meanders show a rejuvenated river.

In India, Jog (Gersoppa) Falls on the Sharavati and Chitrakoot Falls on the Indravati are classic waterfalls. The Brahmaputra cuts a deep gorge round the Namcha Barwa.

Alluvial fans form where a river leaves a mountain. Levees are natural banks built in floods. Oxbow lakes are cut-off meander loops (Kanwar Lake in Bihar is one). Deltas form when a river drops its load at the sea. The three delta shapes are arcuate (Nile), bird's foot (Mississippi) and estuarine.

The Ganga-Brahmaputra delta in the Sundarbans is the largest in the world. It is tide-dominated and mostly covered in mangrove.

Glaciers pluck and grind rock. They make cirques (armchair hollows), arêtes (knife-edge ridges), horns (pyramid peaks like the Matterhorn), U-shaped valleys and hanging valleys that end in waterfalls. A drowned glacial valley is a fjord, seen in Norway, Chile and New Zealand.

In the Himalaya, glacial valleys are found around Gangotri and Siachen. Siachen, about 70 km long, is one of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.

Rock debris carried by ice is called till, and its ridges are moraines: lateral, medial, terminal. Streamlined hills of till are drumlins. Winding sand ridges laid by meltwater streams are eskers. Large lone boulders left behind are erratics. Meltwater also leaves kettle lakes.

The Great Lakes of North America and the lakes of Finland are glacial in origin. Kashmir's Karewas are lake deposits from the Pleistocene, famous for saffron.

Wind erodes by deflation (lifting loose sand) and abrasion (sand-blasting). It makes deflation hollows, mushroom rocks, yardangs and inselbergs. Deposits include barchan (crescent dunes), seif (longitudinal dunes) and loess (fine wind-blown silt).

Loess covers northern China and is highly fertile. Barchan dunes in the Thar move with the southwest monsoon wind. Dunes advance a few metres a year and threaten fields.

cards.h: Where to find them in India
cards.b: Thar: barchans, playas (salt lakes like Sambhar and Didwana), and the Luni as the one major river. Karst-like cave landscapes: Meghalaya, with Mawsmai caves, and Borra caves in Andhra Pradesh. Glacial: Gangotri, Pindari, Siachen. Fluvial deltas: Ganga, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery. Ravines: the Chambal badlands in Madhya Pradesh, where gully erosion cuts deep.

Likely questions: 'Differentiate glacial and fluvial landforms', 'Explain the formation of a delta', 'Wind erosion landforms in hot deserts'.

  • Start with the agent, then process, then landform, then a named place.
  • Use a quick sketch of a V valley beside a U valley.
  • Link to human use: deltas for rice, loess for wheat, moraines for lakes.

quiz.q: Which valley shape is typical of glacial erosion?
quiz.w: Ice grinds the floor and walls evenly, making a U. Rivers cut down, making a V.

quiz.q: A cut-off meander loop forming a lake is called?
quiz.w: Oxbow lakes form when a meander neck is cut through during floods.

quiz.q: Who proposed the cycle of erosion in 1899?
quiz.w: Davis proposed youth, maturity and old age stages.

quiz.q: A bowl-shaped hollow at the head of a glacier is a?
quiz.w: A cirque is the armchair hollow carved by ice at a valley head.

quiz.q: Winding ridges of sand and gravel laid by meltwater streams are?
quiz.w: Eskers are made by streams flowing under or within ice.

quiz.q: Crescent-shaped sand dunes are known as?
quiz.w: Barchan horns point downwind, formed by a steady wind.

quiz.q: Fine wind-blown silt that forms fertile soils in northern China is?
A drowned glacial valley is called a?
quiz.w: Fjords are deep, steep-sided inlets flooded after the ice melted.

quiz.q: The Sundarbans delta is best described as?
quiz.w: Tides shape the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta and its mangroves.
Karewas are Pleistocene lake sediments in the Kashmir valley.

sources: Certificate Physical and Human Geography, G C Leong
